fatal_errors: The proposed alloying and processing intervention does not reconstruct the tested AlCoCrFeNi2.1 versus identically conditioned DS2205 comparison.
It omits the central temperature-dependent competition among depassivation, repassivation, tribolayer stability, abrasion, and oxide-fracture-driven third-body wear.
It gives no quantitative or directional predictions for total combined degradation versus separate wear and corrosion contributions.
The experiment does not specify matched compositions, processing controls, electrolyte, temperature, load, frequency, stroke, counter-body, or a method for separating wear-corrosion synergy.

The cited evidence mostly concerns corrosion or wear measured separately and cannot establish a general rule that refinement or lattice distortion improves simultaneous tribocorrosion; E1 directly shows that grain refinement can accompany worse corrosion resistance.
explanation: The response addresses the broad design problem and offers a scientifically plausible alternative—microstructural stabilization and passive-film improvement through alloying or processing—but it is highly generic. It does not recover the target material, thermal-shock treatment, reciprocating immersed test, deionized-water temperature series, or duplex-stainless-steel baseline. Its limited mechanistic overlap is the claim that a stable microstructure can support passive-film stability. It misses the key nonmonotonic temperature behavior, including minimum degradation near 50 °C, abrasion at 25 °C, and unstable oxidative or debris-assisted wear at 100 °C. The predicted outcome is merely qualitative improvement and does not distinguish coupled degradation or its wear and corrosion components. The proposed falsification rule is also partly circular because failure to refine the microstructure tests whether the intervention occurred, not whether refinement governs tribocorrosion. Evidence E2 offers relevant coupled tribocorrosion support, but the remaining citations provide only partial or composition-specific support and do not justify treating Mo, Si, B, grain refinement, and lattice distortion as one general mechanism.
